questions.stem: A teacher gives a half-done example to child while teaching a particular concept. According to Lev Vygotsky’s which of the following strategies is the teacher using"
questions.explanation: The strategy described, where a teacher gives a half-done example to a child while teaching a particular concept, aligns with scaffolding according to Lev Vygotsky's theory. This approach allows students to achieve tasks they would not be able to accomplish on their own, effectively bridging the gap within their Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD).

questions.stem: One of the main characteristics of pre- operational thought according to Jean Piaget is which refers to the tendency to focus on one aspect of a situation and neglect others.
questions.explanation: Centration is one of the main characteristics of pre-operational thought in Jean Piaget’s theory of cognitive development. It refers to the tendency of children at this stage to focus on one aspect of a situation while neglecting or ignoring other relevant aspects. For example, if you show a pre-operational child two glasses of liquid, one tall and narrow and the other short and wide, and pour the contents of one glass into a different-shaped glass, the child may think that the amount of liquid has changed simply because of the change in appearance (centrating on appearance) rather than recognizing that the amount remains the same (conservation).
questions.supporting_excerpt: One of the main characteristics of pre- operational thought according to Jean Piaget is which refers to the tendency to focus on one aspect of a situation and neglect others. — Answer: (B) Centration

questions.explanation: Inner speech, also known as private speech or self-talk, is a concept in Vygotsky’s theory that suggests children use speech (talking to oneself) as a tool for cognitive development and selfregulation. Inner speech allows children to plan, guide, and monitor their actions and thoughts, ultimately helping them solve problems and think more independently. It's a way for children to regulate and improve their own thinking processes as they transition from external to internal modes of cognitive control.

questions.stem: Four-year-old Aparna says that a button is alive because it helps tie her shirt together. According to Jean Piaget, her thinking is characterized by :
questions.explanation: Animistic thinking is a cognitive characteristic of preoperational thought in Piaget’s theory. It involves attributing human-like qualities, such as life and intentions, to inanimate objects or natural phenomena. In this case, Aparna attributes the quality of being "alive" to a button because it helps her tie her shirt together. This reflects her tendency to anthropomor- phize or treat non-living things as if they have human characteristics.
